ex.im.Jco06: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.Jco06.hint: No check or capture wins material. In the list, the seventh rank is your imbalance.
ex.im.Jco06.solution: 29.Raa7! It is neither check nor capture: it is the plan from the list. The rook on a5 goes to the seventh rank and doubles with the one on d7. After 29...Kh8 30.Rxg7, the two rooks on the seventh hem in the black king, and White has a decisive advantage.
ex.im.DgQKh: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.im.DgQKh.hint: Your knight on d4 stands on an outpost, on the file of the rook on d8 and the white king.
ex.im.DgQKh.solution: 25...Nxf3#! The outpost knight captures on f3 and gives check, and the rook on d8 also gives check along the d-file: it is double check. The bishop on b3 controls c2 and d1, the knight controls e1, and the pawn on f4 controls e3.
ex.im.XWldS: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.XWldS.hint: Your rook is on the seventh rank, and the knight on g5 hems in the black king.
ex.im.XWldS.solution: 42.Rf7#! The rook on the seventh rank goes to f7 and gives mate along the f-file. The knight on g5 controls e4 and e6, the pawn on f4 controls e5 and g5, and the pawn on h3 controls g4.
ex.im.Lkgyl: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.im.Lkgyl.hint: Your bishop pair has open diagonals to the white king, and the rook on d8 is on the open d-file.
ex.im.Lkgyl.solution: 17...Bc4#! The bishop on e6 goes to c4 and gives mate. The bishop on b4 controls d2 and e1, the rook on d8 controls d1 and d3, and the bishop on c4 controls f1. Together, the two bishops cover squares of both colours around the king.
ex.im.gCHam: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.gCHam.hint: In the list, your strongest imbalance is on the queenside, near the black queen on b7.
ex.im.gCHam.solution: 30.a6! The passed pawn advances and attacks the queen on b7. After 30...Rxa1 31.axb7, the pawn threatens to queen on b8. If 31...Rb1, 32.Ra8+ Kf7 33.b8=Q, and White has a decisive advantage.
ex.im.1kgLE: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.1kgLE.hint: Your bishop pair and the rook on the seventh rank hem in the black king.
ex.im.1kgLE.solution: 33.Bh7+! The bishop on f5 goes to h7 with check, defended by the rook on d7. After 33...Kf8 34.Bg7#, the other bishop gives mate: the bishop on h7 controls g8, and the rook on the seventh rank controls e7 and f7 and defends the bishop on g7.
ex.im.hdg4M: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.hdg4M.hint: Your rook on d1 stands on the d-file, half-open, and the pawn on d7 stands between it and the black king.
ex.im.hdg4M.solution: 29.Ne6+! The knight gives check and attacks the rook on c7. The pawn on d7 cannot capture it: the rook on d1 pins it to the king along the d-file. After 29...Kc8 30.Nxc7, White wins the rook.
ex.im.xX3J9: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.xX3J9.hint: No check or capture wins material yet. In the list, the passed pawn on d7 and the open e-file are yours.
ex.im.xX3J9.solution: 31.Rde2! It is neither check nor capture: the rooks double on the open e-file. After 31...Rd6 32.Re8+, the rook on e2 defends e8; if 32...Rxe8, 33.dxe8=Q#, and after 32...Kf7 33.Rxd8, White wins a rook. Without doubling, 31.Re8+? Rxe8 32.dxe8=Q+ Kxe8 only trades the pieces.
ex.im.uFoDf: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.im.uFoDf.hint: The black knight on c1 is far from the other black pieces. Look for a check that opens your rook's path to it.
ex.im.uFoDf.solution: 44.Rxc6+! The rook captures the pawn on c6 with check and opens the c-file. After 44...Kf7 45.Rxc1, it goes down the open file and captures the knight, and White has a decisive advantage.
part.imbalances.title: Imbalances
part.imbalances.summary: In a quiet position, the plan comes from the differences between the two sides: pawns, pieces, squares and files. With a tactic in the position, calculate before making the list.
part.prophylaxis.title: Prophylaxis
part.prophylaxis.summary: In a quiet position, before playing your plan, ask what the opponent wants to do and take that move away. First, check the checks and captures.
ex.pf.own1: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.own1.hint: What does Black want to do with the knight on a2? See which squares it would use to get out.
ex.pf.own1.solution: 1.Kd2! The king covers c1 and defends the c3 pawn, and the c3 pawn covers b4: the knight on a2 has no way out. Next, the king goes to c2 and wins the knight. After 1.Kd1?, the knight captures the c3 pawn with check and escapes.
ex.pf.own2: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.own2.hint: Where does the b8 knight want to go, and what would it do there?
ex.pf.own2.solution: 1.b5! The b8 knight wanted to go to c6 to trade your d4 knight, and the pawn ending left would be a draw. With the pawn on b5, c6 is covered and the black knight has no move. Your far more active knight stays on the board, and the black pawns soon start to fall.
ex.pf.own4: Play as Black and find the best move.
ex.pf.own4.hint: Your king has no escape square. Before making one, look at the white king too.
ex.pf.own4.solution: 1...Re1#! The white king has no escape square either, and no white piece covers the first rank: it is a back-rank mate. With 1...h6?, the prophylactic move, White would also make a square for the king, and the mate would be gone.
ex.pf.RxgNx: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.RxgNx.hint: The black bishop on a2 is far from its own pieces. Which way does it want to come back?
ex.pf.RxgNx.solution: 1.b3! With the pawn on b3, the a2 bishop is surrounded: the c2 queen covers b1 and defends b3. If it captures on b3, 2.Qxb3, and White wins a piece for a pawn.
ex.pf.own3: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.own3.hint: What does Black want to do against your e4 knight?
ex.pf.own3.solution: 1.g4! Black wanted to play 1...f5 and drive your knight from e4. On that square the dark-squared bishop cannot reach it, and the black pawns on c5, e5, f6 and h6 stand on dark squares, in that bishop's way. With the pawn on g4, a pawn that goes to f5 is captured: the knight stays on e4, and your king comes closer calmly.
ex.pf.mxRiC: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.mxRiC.hint: Black wants to drive your f4 bishop away with the g7 pawn. Before stopping that, see whether the position already has a tactic.
ex.pf.mxRiC.solution: 1.Ng6+! The knight gives check. If the h7 pawn captures it, the h-file opens, and 2.Qh3 is mate. With 1.h4?, the prophylaxis against the pawn going to g5, Black would trade the d6 bishop for your knight, and the chance would be gone.
ex.pf.jukuD: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.jukuD.hint: The black rook on g2 is in your camp. Which way does it want to get out?
ex.pf.jukuD.solution: 1.Rh1! The g2 rook wanted to get out through h2. Your rook covers h2 and g1, and the king defends the f2 pawn: the black rook has no way out. After 1...Rxg3+, 2.fxg3 wins the rook for a pawn.
ex.pf.LeK02: Play as White and find the best move.
ex.pf.LeK02.hint: The bishop on b6 has few squares. After your move, check what Black threatens.
ex.pf.LeK02.solution: 1.a5! The pawn attacks the b6 bishop, which has no safe square: on c5, the b2 pawn goes to b4 and traps it. Black hits back with 1...Bh3, against the g2 pawn, defended only by the king, with the g8 rook behind. 2.g3! closes the g-file, and the a5 pawn still attacks the bishop. After 2...Bxf1 3.Bxf1, the pawn captures on b6: White gets two pieces for the rook. After 2.axb6?, the rook captures on g2 with check, and the attack belongs to Black.
